gbm_population_evidence.quote: Biopsy proven high-grade glioma (HGG) as defined by 2016 World Health Organization (WHO) Classification Criteria, Grade 3-4 including:

candidate_evidence.quote: The purpose of this study is to measure the benefit of adding abemaciclib to the chemotherapy, temozolomide, for newly diagnosed high-grade glioma following radiotherapy.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: A Randomized, Open-Label, Phase 2 Study Evaluating Abemaciclib in Combination With Temozolomide Compared to Temozolomide Monotherapy in Children and Young Adults With Newly Diagnosed High-Grade Glioma Following Radiotherapy

role_evidence.quote: Participants will receive abemaciclib administered orally in addition to temozolomide administered orally or intravenously (IV).
Participants will receive temozolomide administered orally or IV.

source_quote.quote: IDH-mutant astrocytoma with homozygous CDKN2A/B deletion

flag.reason: CDKN2A/B deletion appears only as part of the definition of one of many eligible diagnoses (not a trial-wide requirement); coded not matched, but a CDK4/6 inhibitor with CDKN2A/B deletion could be read as candidate-matched enrichment.

coder_notes: Paediatric/young adult HGG trial (ages CHILD, ADULT) that lists glioblastoma among several eligible HGG diagnoses under both WHO 2016 and WHO 2021 definitions (cns5 chosen as both are cited). Only the IDH-mutant astrocytoma diagnosis carries the CDKN2A/B requirement; other molecular diagnoses (H3, IDH) are histopathological categories and not listed. ALK/BRAF/NTRK appear only in exclusion criteria. Abemaciclib PK is plasma only.
